claims.text: Adding titanium and aluminum to the alloy will produce in-situ TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles.
The in-situ TiC and Al2O3 particles will reinforce the alloy.
Dispersion strengthening by the particles will improve high-temperature mechanical capability.
The modified alloy will exhibit a 25% improvement in high-temperature mechanical capability relative to an as-cast refractory high-entropy alloy without reinforcement particles.
The predicted improvement will hold at 1000°C under a mechanical loading condition of 500 MPa.
The intervention will increase density by less than 5% relative to the baseline.
The intervention will preserve room-temperature performance.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis requires a density increase below 5%, but the experiment only falsifies it when density increases by more than 10%, leaving outcomes between 5% and 10% that violate the stated boundary without falsifying the hypothesis.
The predicted improvement is 25%, whereas falsification occurs only below 15%; an improvement from 15% to below 25% would fail the quantitative prediction but would not falsify the hypothesis.
